name: Invariant σ-algebra of a measure-preserving transformation
description: For a measure-preserving map T on (Ω,F,P), the sub-σ-field 𝓘 = {A ∈ F : T⁻¹A = A} of T-invariant events, whose triviality (mod P) characterizes ergodicity of T.

name: σ-algebra generated by a random variable
description: For a measurable map X : (Ω,F) → (S,𝓢), the smallest sub-σ-field σ(X) = X⁻¹(𝓢) = {X⁻¹(B) : B ∈ 𝓢} making X measurable, encoding exactly the information carried by X.

name: Stieltjes measure function
description: A nondecreasing right-continuous function F : ℝ → ℝ that induces a unique Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure μ on (ℝ,𝓑) via μ((a,b]) = F(b) − F(a).

name: Feller's converse to the central limit theorem
description: For a uniformly asymptotically negligible triangular array whose row sums converge to a standard normal, the Lindeberg condition is necessary, i.e. asymptotic normality with negligible summands forces Lindeberg's condition to hold.

name: Esseen's smoothing inequality
description: Bounds the sup-norm distance between two distribution functions (one with bounded density) by an integral of the difference of their characteristic functions over a finite frequency window plus a remainder, supplying the analytic engine for Berry–Esseen-type rates.

name: Lindeberg replacement (swapping) method
function_signature: (Sum of independent summands, smooth test function f) → (CLT error bound via term-by-term Gaussian substitution)
description: Proves a central limit theorem by replacing the summands one at a time with matching-moment Gaussians and Taylor-expanding a smooth test function, telescoping the total error into a sum of small third-order remainders.

name: Standard machine (measure-theoretic bootstrap)
function_signature: (Property verified for indicators) → (Property for all integrable measurable functions)
description: Establishes a linear/monotone identity or inequality for general measurable functions by proving it first for indicator functions, then extending by linearity to simple functions, by monotone convergence to nonnegative measurable functions, and finally by difference to integrable functions.

name: Mixing implies ergodicity
description: Any (strongly or weakly) mixing measure-preserving transformation is ergodic, since asymptotic independence P(A ∩ T⁻ⁿB) → P(A)P(B) forces every invariant set to have measure 0 or 1.

name: Kolmogorov cycle condition
description: An irreducible positive-recurrent Markov chain with stationary distribution is reversible if and only if for every finite cycle x₀ → x₁ → … → xₙ = x₀ the product of forward transition probabilities equals the product of the reverse transition probabilities.
